practiceReport.name: Abraham Lucas
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (92% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: Per John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters Wednesday that Lucas is not a candidate for injured reserve but is expected to miss "days to weeks" due to an ankle sprain that he suffered in Week 10 against the Raiders. Josh Jones, Bobby Hart and Chase Lundt are all candidates to start at right tackle for as long as Lucas is sidelined.

practiceReport.name: Quenton Nelson
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (9th NFL season, 99% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: Nelson underwent a minor procedure on his knee in early November and will be sidelined for a second consecutive game. He's had additional time to rest thanks to the Seahawks' Week 11 bye, and Macdonald relayed Wednesday that the team is "hopeful" that Nelson will be cleared to return for Week 13 against the Cowboys on Monday, Dec. 7. Greg Zabel will likely start at left guard in Nelson's absence.

practiceReport.name: Terrion Arnold
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (CB) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: It was reported earlier this month that Arnold would be joining the Seahawks, and the move became official Saturday. Per Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network, Arnold will be placed on the commissioner's exempt list while he works through legal issues stemming from an incident in June, so it's unclear when he will be ready to see action with his new team.

practiceReport.name: Jarran Reed
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Trench/box position (DT) — historically higher active rate through braced upper-body & ankle soreness (81% baseline).
factors: Did Not Participate (DNP) on Wednesday (veteran maintenance profile, awaiting Thursday workload)
practiceReport.beatComment: Reed limped off the field during the first half and was subsequently deemed doubtful to return. Brandon Pili should get a lot more defensive snaps in the likely scenario that Reed is unable to re-enter Sunday's contest.

practiceReport.name: Sam Darnold
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (9th NFL season, 87% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.
practiceReport.beatComment: Head coach Mike Macdonald told Brady Henderson of ESPN.com on Wednesday that Darnold will start Sunday at San Francisco if he fares well in practice this week, and a full practice is a good place for the quarterback to kick things off. Darnold has missed the last two contests due to a quad injury and cracked ribs, but only the first concern was mentioned on Wednesday's practice report, indicating his improved level of health.

irAndReserveTracker.name: George Holani
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Holani was knocked out of the Seahawks' last game in Week 10 at Las Vegas due to a knee injury that eventually was deemed to be an MCL sprain. Per Brady Henderson of ESPN.com, head coach Mike Macdonald said he was uncertain if Holani will require surgery, but the running back will be sidelined for at least four games by virtue of landing on IR. In the meantime, Emanuel Wilson will serve as the team's No. 3 back behind Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Bud Clark
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: 4-game minimum satisfied on Injured Reserve (Ankle); awaiting 21-day practice window designation.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Julian Neal
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Neal was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the 49ers due to a hamstring injury, which is severe enough for the rookie third-rounder to warrant a stint on injured reserve. As such, Neal will be forced to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 9 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 8. He's mostly operated on special teams this season, but his absence will also weaken the Seahawks' depth in the secondary.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Elijah Arroyo
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Macdonald didn't outright rule Arroyo out for the entire 2026 campaign, leaving the possibility that the second-year tight end would be available if the Seahawks made a deep playoff run. Regardless, Arroyo will not be available for the rest of the regular season while recovering from a shoulder injury, leaving Eric Saubert and Nick Kallerup as the Seahawks' depth options at tight end behind AJ Barner.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jake Bobo
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Bobo sustained a serious knee injury in Friday's joint practice with the Titans. The wide receiver's placement on injured reserve means he will be unable to participate for the Seahawks in the entirety of the 2026 season. With Bobo out of the picture, Tory Horton (undisclosed), Emmanuel Henderson, Montorie Foster and Cody White will have a close competition for starting roles during the remainder of the preseason. The Seahawks also signed wide receiver Julian Hicks in a corresponding move.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Mason Richman
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Richman suffered a serious right leg injury during Sunday's preseason loss to the Titans. The offensive lineman will now miss the entirety of the 2026 regular season unless he is waived with an injury settlement. The second-year player maintained his depth role on the offensive line throughout his rookie season and will have to fight for the same status in 2027.
